claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a Christian priest (presbyter) of the Church of Jerusalem.
Hesychius of Jerusalem was active during the first half of the fifth century, approximately from the 410s to the 450s.
Hesychius served as a priest in the church in Jerusalem around 412 and was recognized by 429 as the pre-eminent biblical interpreter and teacher of the church in Jerusalem and Palestine.
The work In sanctum Procopium (Homily 14) is a homily in praise of Saint Procopius the Persian, a martyr.
The homily was composed and preached during the feast of Procopius in Jerusalem.
The homily was written in Greek at Jerusalem in the early 5th century.
Procopius was a martyr of Caesarea in Palestine.
The homily compares Procopius to various biblical figures including Paul, John the Evangelist, Elijah, Samuel, Samson, David, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Enoch, and Job.
The homily includes exhortations to the audience and discussion of biblical quotations related to martyrdom and perseverance.
The homily is catalogued as CPG 6578 and BHG 1584 in standard patristic bibliographies.
Hesychius was a renowned preacher and his homilies were part of his celebrated literary output.
